newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia details terms of auction of 2 energy firms.
newsitem.headline: Russia details terms of auction of 2 energy firms.

text.p: Auctions of state stakes in two Russian energy companies, KomiTEK and East-Siberian Oil and Gas Company, will be opened on July 1, the Federal Securities Corporation said in a statement on Monday.

The Federal Property Fund said on Friday that auctions of government stakes in the two companies would be opened on July 2, and that the starting date for auctions in four other energy companies had yet to be decided.

The corporation, which is organising the auctions on behalf of the fund, said that 21.7 percent of the charter capital in AO KomiTEK would be up for sale, and that the auction would be open to bids until August 22.
The fund will decide the winner, or winners, of the auction no later than September 19.
The starting price for each of the 36.05 million KomiTEK shares up for auction was set at 3,000 roubles. The shares are nominally valued at 10 roubles each.

The corporation also said 38 percent of the charter capital of AO Vostochno-Sibirskaya Neftegazovaya Kompaniya (East-Siberian Oil and Gas Co) was up for auction, and that the auction would remain open to bids until September 12.
The winner, or winners, of the auction will be chosen no later than October 10.
The starting price for each of the 6.50 million East-Siberian Oil and Gas Co shares up for auction was set at 12,000 roubles. The shares are nominally valued at 20 roubles each.
The companies on offer in addition to KomiTEK and East-Siberian Oil and Gas are the Tyumen Oil Company, Eastern Oil Company, Norsi-Oil and the Siberian-Urals Oil Company (SIBUR).
